source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Limit activity to gentle stretching because moderate aerobic exercise is discouraged even when pregnancy is uncomplicated and no contraindication is present.","B":"Aim for about 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity each week when there are no obstetric or medical contraindications, adjusting activity as needed.","C":"Maintain the pre-pregnancy intensity target without adjusting for symptoms or obstetric changes because exercise recommendations remain fixed throughout pregnancy.","D":"Begin vigorous conditioning even if previously sedentary because pregnancy is an appropriate time to increase exercise intensity rapidly for cardiovascular benefit."}}
source_row.rationale: For a healthy person with an uncomplicated pregnancy and no contraindications, regular physical activity is safe and desirable. Option B is correct because ACOG recommends about 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week, with adjustment as needed. Option A is unnecessarily restrictive. Option C ignores symptoms and obstetric changes. Option D inappropriately recommends rapid progression to vigorous conditioning for someone who may have been sedentary.
source_row.source_detail: ACOG — Exercise During Pregnancy: in uncomplicated pregnancy without medical/obstetric contraindications, physical activity is safe and desirable; pregnant individuals should generally obtain at least 150 minutes of moderate-intensity aerobic activity per week, with activity individualized and adjusted for symptoms/clinical changes. Current ACOG Exercise During Pregnancy patient/professional guidance live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Health Promotion and Maintenance: preventive care, immunization, pregnancy health promotion, adherence support and age/risk-appropriate teaching activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
